headline: How a Failed Video Game Led to Slack

sentences.text: Stewart Butterfield started a company named Tiny Speck.
The team made an online game named Glitch.
The online game did not make money for the team.
The workers used a quiet chat tool for their work.
They changed that message tool into a program named Slack.

grammar.title: Negative Past Tense
grammar.note: In the past tense, we use 'did not' followed by the base verb 'make'. It shows that an action did not happen in the past.

sentences.text: Stewart Butterfield created a business named Tiny Speck to make games.
The team launched an online game named Glitch in late 2011.
The game was not making money, so Butterfield stopped it in 2012.
The workers built a simple chat tool to talk and send files.
They turned this message tool into a new product called Slack.
Many office workers will use this tool to talk with each other.

grammar.title: Infinitive of Purpose
grammar.note: The phrase 'to make' explains the reason behind the action. It answers why Butterfield created the business.

grammar.title: Past Continuous Tense
grammar.note: We use 'was/were + verb-ing' to describe an ongoing situation in the past. Here, it shows that the game was continuously failing to earn money.

sentences.text: Stewart Butterfield founded a company named Tiny Speck to create an online video game.
The company released a game called Glitch, which was not financially successful.
While making the game, workers created an internal chat tool to send text and files.
In late 2012, Butterfield stopped the game and changed the direction of his business.
They turned their private communication system into Slack, launching it publicly in August 2013.
The name Slack stands for Searchable Log of All Conversation and Knowledge.

grammar.title: Non-defining Relative Clause
grammar.note: This clause gives extra detail about the game Glitch. It starts with 'which' and is separated from the main sentence by a comma.

grammar.title: Participle Phrase
grammar.note: An -ing clause attached to the end of a sentence describes a related secondary action. It adds background information about how or when the main event occurred.

sentences.text: A company named Tiny Speck, led by Stewart Butterfield, originally developed an online game named Glitch.
Although Glitch launched in 2011, Butterfield realized by October 2012 that it would not be profitable.
Consequently, the company decided to shut down the game and repurpose its internal communication tools.
The internal chat software had been built to automate file exchanges and organize messages among developers.
Butterfield explained that the name Slack came from Searchable Log of All Conversation and Knowledge.
Following a public release in August 2013, Tiny Speck was renamed Slack Technologies to match its focus.
The cloud enterprise software firm Salesforce eventually acquired Slack in July 2021 for approximately 27.7 billion dollars.

grammar.title: Future in the Past
grammar.note: 'Would' acts as the past form of 'will' when looking ahead from a past point in time. Butterfield realized back in 2012 that the game was not going to be profitable later.

grammar.title: Past Perfect Passive
grammar.note: The pattern 'had been + past participle' describes an action completed before another past point. It shows the software was built before the team decided to repurpose it.

sentences.text: When Stewart Butterfield founded Tiny Speck to create the browser game Glitch, the company focused on building an online multiplayer experience.
Despite launching in late 2011, the video game suffered from accessibility issues and was deemed financially unviable by October 2012.
Instead of continuing the struggling title, Butterfield shut down Glitch and changed the primary business direction of his company.
The development team salvaged their custom messaging system, which had been constructed around existing chat protocols to handle internal communication.
Designed to organize message threads and automate file transfers, the software was repurposed and officially launched to the public in August 2013.
Butterfield revealed that the distinct name Slack served as an acronym standing for Searchable Log of All Conversation and Knowledge.
Tiny Speck subsequently renamed itself Slack Technologies, fully reorienting its business around the rapidly growing workplace chat platform.
In July 2021, enterprise software provider Salesforce finalized its acquisition of Slack for approximately 27.7 billion dollars.

grammar.title: Passive Voice with Complement
grammar.note: The passive construction 'was deemed' is followed by an adjective phrase serving as a subject complement. It describes how the game was evaluated by its creators.

grammar.title: Reflexive Pronoun as Object
grammar.note: Reflexive pronouns like 'itself' are used when the subject and object refer to the same entity. Here, Tiny Speck performed the action of renaming on itself.
